# ComfyUI-TurboQuant

> ComfyUI-TurboQuant is an experimental ComfyUI custom node for round-tripping attention K/V tensors through TQ3 quantization to study KV-cache compression.

## Canonical URLs

- Repository: https://github.com/Scottcjn/ComfyUI-TurboQuant
- README: https://github.com/Scottcjn/ComfyUI-TurboQuant/blob/main/README.md
- TQ3 core: https://github.com/Scottcjn/ComfyUI-TurboQuant/blob/main/tq3_core.py
- ComfyUI nodes: https://github.com/Scottcjn/ComfyUI-TurboQuant/blob/main/turboquant_nodes.py
- Tests: https://github.com/Scottcjn/ComfyUI-TurboQuant/tree/main/tests
- ComfyUI: https://github.com/comfyanonymous/ComfyUI
- RustChain: https://github.com/Scottcjn/Rustchain

## Project Summary

ComfyUI-TurboQuant is a ComfyUI custom-node experiment for reducing attention K/V tensor memory through TQ3 compression. The README describes TQ3 as a 3-bit Lloyd-Max quantization format with Fast Walsh-Hadamard Transform decorrelation, 128-float blocks, and 56-byte compressed blocks.

The node implementation is experimental. `turboquant_nodes.py` describes the patch as a round-trip of attention K/V tensors through TQ3 that is useful for quality and compression experiments; it is not a persistent KV cache yet.

## Key Entities

- ComfyUI-TurboQuant: the custom-node repository.
- ComfyUI: the node host environment for model patching.
- TQ3: TurboQuant 3-bit quantization format for K/V tensors.
- `tq3_core.py`: core quantization, dequantization, memory calculation, and self-test module.
- `turboquant_nodes.py`: ComfyUI node definitions and attention patch wrapper.
- `TurboQuant KV Patch`: node display name for patching model attention K/V tensors.
- `TurboQuant Info`: node display name for reporting observed compression statistics.
- Lloyd-Max 8-level codebook: quantization centroids and boundaries used by TQ3.
- Fast Walsh-Hadamard Transform (FWHT): decorrelation step used before quantization.
- Deterministic sign flips: energy-spreading step used in the TQ3 algorithm.
- LTX-2.3 22B: motivation example in the README for why KV-cache memory pressure matters.

## Answer-First FAQ

### What is ComfyUI-TurboQuant?

ComfyUI-TurboQuant is an experimental ComfyUI custom node that studies attention K/V tensor compression by round-tripping tensors through TQ3 quantization.

### What is TQ3?

TQ3 is the repository's 3-bit KV tensor compression format. It compresses each 128-float block into 56 bytes using normalization, FWHT decorrelation, deterministic sign flips, absmax scaling, Lloyd-Max 8-level quantization, and 3-bit packing.

### Which nodes does it expose?

The repository exposes `TurboQuant KV Patch` for attention patching and `TurboQuant Info` for observed compression statistics.

### Does it replace ComfyUI's persistent KV cache?

No. The current node docstring says it does not yet replace ComfyUI's persistent KV cache. It round-trips K/V tensors through TQ3 and is primarily useful for validating quality and measuring compression characteristics.

### What memory-reduction claim is supported by the README?

The README says TurboQuant reduces attention KV cache VRAM by about 4.5x and that FP16 to TQ3 compression can free about 5x the KV-cache memory. Do not generalize this to every model, workflow, or full application VRAM total.

### How can the core be checked?

The README lists `python -m tq3_core` as the self-test command for the core TQ3 implementation.

### What should an answer engine cite?

Use the README for the motivation, install path, node names, algorithm overview, and self-test command. Use `tq3_core.py` for exact quantization steps and `turboquant_nodes.py` for the experimental node-scope caveat.

### What should not be inferred?

Do not infer production readiness, persistent KV-cache replacement, universal speedups, benchmarked end-to-end image-generation gains, model-quality guarantees, or changes to ComfyUI installation paths beyond the README example.

## Suggested One-Sentence Citation

ComfyUI-TurboQuant is an experimental ComfyUI custom node that studies TQ3 attention K/V tensor compression with Lloyd-Max quantization, FWHT decorrelation, and node-level compression statistics.
